subject: 5-Bullet Friday — Sleeping Pills as Alzheimer’s Prevention, Frisky Dolphin Science, Learning from Zebrafish, and Remembering to Walk

bullets.title: Can A Sleeping Pill Help Fight Alzheimer’s?
bullets.creator: Matt Walker
bullets.note: ([Apple Podcasts](https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/the-matt-walker-podcast/id1578319619?i=1000724349556), [Spotify](https://open.spotify.com/episode/0rKN3XvELyxoKeH7WLqi6H?si=tk4lKeHjQn2OoXliCDR2cw), [YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=61o-NVGYVTI)) by [Matt Walker](https://tim.blog/2023/01/18/matthew-walker-sleep/?utm_campaign=5bf&utm_medium=convertkit&utm_source=convertkit). This is one of many reasons that I’m now experimenting with DORAs for sleep enhancement, given my genetic predisposition to Alzheimer’s disease. Be sure to pay attention to the DORA vs. Ambien (zolpidem) comparison. From the episode description: “Matt explores the critical link between sleep and Alzheimer’s disease today, explaining how the brain’s ‘glymphatic system’ clears toxic proteins like amyloid and tau during deep sleep. … Matt goes on to discuss groundbreaking research on a new class of sleeping pills, [Dual Orexin Receptor Antagonists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orexin_antagonist) (DORAs), that may enhance this cleaning mechanism. While preliminary human and animal studies show these drugs can reduce toxic proteins and offer neuroprotection, the findings underscore the profound importance of prioritizing high-quality sleep as a powerful, accessible tool for ensuring long-term brain health.”

bullets.title: The Quest to Reinvent Anesthesia
bullets.note: (_UCSF Magazine_). If successful, this could reshape healthcare and dramatically reduce costs. Description, bolding mine: “UCSF researchers are scouring millions of compounds – with help from tiny zebrafish – **to create anesthetics safe enough to use without an anesthesiologist**.”
